- If sentiment is consistently negative (0.00 or low) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- If model shows gradual upward trend (e.g., +0.1–0.3 per day) but true outcome drops sharply, model is lagging — anticipate sharper decline and reduce forecast slope early.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >85), model often overshoots and continues rising — cap forecast at 1–2% above peak or add a downward correction factor if sentiment turns negative.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.5–0.67), model tends to be overly conservative — allow 0.5–1.0% above forecast to capture mean reversion or volatility.
- If true outcome is below 70 and model is still rising, model is ignoring fundamental downward pressure — reduce forecast slope or add a floor at 68–70.
- If sentiment is positive (1.00) but model is flat or declining, model is underreacting — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to reflect sentiment bias.
- Model often underestimates volatility in early 30d horizon — add 0.5–1.0% buffer if sentiment is volatile or recent price action is erratic.
